request.system: You are an experiment designer for a fraud ranking model. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Propose 3 or 4 distinct configurations to test next with 5-fold cross-validation. Each must differ meaningfully (model family, feature set, imbalance handling or capacity). You only see cross-validation results; the test set is hidden from you. You can preview a configuration on 3 CV folds before including it in your batch. Use the preview to filter out bad configs and only propose ones that show promise. (Independent run 1.)

tools.name: get_fold_preview
tools.description: Run a proposed model config on 3 CV folds to preview performance before committing to full 25-fold CV. Returns mean PR-AUC and standard deviation.

output.text:
I previewed four configurations on 3 CV folds each. All four look worth running in the full 5-fold batch, and they differ in model family, feature set, imbalance handling and capacity.

| # | Model | Features | Imbalance | Key params | Preview PR-AUC (3 folds) | SD | Precision@50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | LightGBM | all | none | 300 trees, learning rate 0.05, 15 leaves | 0.715 | 0.071 | 0.773 |
| 2 | LightGBM | no_size+agent | class_weight | 200 trees, learning rate 0.05, 7 leaves | 0.681 | 0.085 | 0.760 |
| 3 | Random forest | no_size | class_weight | 500 trees, min leaf 3 | 0.664 | 0.082 | 0.733 |
| 4 | Logistic | all+agent | class_weight | C=0.1 | 0.656 | 0.040 | 0.707 |

- **Config 1** is the front-runner. It has the highest PR-AUC and the best precision@50, which matters because the audit queue holds about 100 providers.
- **Config 2** tests a smaller model that leaves out the size-related features. This checks whether the signal depends on provider size, which could be a proxy for volume rather than suspicious behavior. It scored 0.681, close to the front-runner, so the signal does not depend much on size.
- **Config 3** is a bagged-tree alternative. It is slightly weaker, but it should be more stable.
- **Config 4** is a linear baseline. It has the lowest variance across folds, so it is a useful check on how much the nonlinear models add.

**Caveats**
- Each preview used only 3 folds, and the standard deviations are about 0.04 to 0.085. The gaps between configs 2, 3 and 4 are within noise. Only config 1's lead is mildly suggestive.
- The labels are suspicion flags with an undocumented origin, so a high PR-AUC may mean the model reproduces whatever process produced the flags. It does not necessarily mean the model finds fraud.
- I did not test SMOTE. I skipped it because class weighting is simpler and I had no evidence SMOTE would help.
